messages:
marta: Heads-up: eucentral1 GPU capacity degrading fast — about 25% of pods marked NotReady after a batch of spot evictions. Latency p95 creeping toward SLO. Starting an emergency mitigation thread. 

marta: Proposed immediate actions: 1) apply per-customer soft caps, 2) divert non-critical customers to other regions, 3) enable burst pool for enterprise tier. Need owners for each. :rotating_light:

devon: I can own the per-customer soft caps. Will push a conservative rule set first (soft limit = 60% of usual) to avoid hard errors.

ash (ops-runner): sre-bot just spiked alerts: 
```
ALERT: node_preemption_rate > 0.2 in eucentral1
affected_nodes: g4-*-preempt
start: 2026-03-18T19:21:12Z
```

ops-runner: Reproducible — cloud reported maintenance window + spot reclaim.

devon: Plan for caps: deploy rate-limit config via policy service. Snippet:
```json
{
  "scope": "customer",
  "rule": "soft_cap",
  "percentage": 60,
  "fallback": "queue-with-backoff"
}
```
I'll roll to 10 heavy customers first.

jen: Which 10? we should exclude customers with SLA >99.9% unless we have explicit exemption.

devon: Good call — excluding enterprise_exempt list. I'll share exact customer IDs in a sec.

kevin: What about ABC-Corp (enterprise, high throughput)? They have dedicated capacity claim — can we route them to reserved pool or burst to us-east-1?

marta: ABC-Corp is on dedicated reservation but the reservation spans eu-central1 only. We can enable temporary cross-region failover to use us-east-1 burst for up to 30% of their traffic. That requires route update and billing opt-in.

ash (ops-runner): I'm running the traffic-shift job now:
```
./traffic-shift --src=eucentral1 --dst=useast1 --customer=ABC-Corp --pct=30 --dry-run=false
```

ops-runner: Job started, seeing initial env checks pass.

sre-bot: [alert] routing-controller: failed to attach ENI for pod inference-queue-67 (retrying)

devon: I've applied the soft-cap policy for customer set A (10 customers). Commands: `policyctl apply --file softcap-cust-a.json`. Monitoring metrics now.

marta: Great. Ops, can you also spin up 4 nodes in burst pool in eu-west-1 and mark them available for cross-region routing? That'll give us headroom while evictions calm down.

ops-runner: Spinning up now. `gcloud compute instances create --count=4 --preemptible ...`

kevin: Any ETA on when evictions stabilize?

ops-runner: Cloud says reclaim wave should finish in ~40m. We're seeing spot reclaim pattern, not systemic network problem.

jen: Dev teams, heads-up: some non-enterprise customers will see increased 429s due to soft caps. Please set client retry backoff to ~1.2x and queue with jitter. Add observability tag `softcap-eucentral1-20260318`.

devon: Metrics after soft-cap rollout (T+5min): per-customer QPS down ~35% for target set, overall p95 latency reduced ~12%. No errors >1% yet.

marta: Good. Ops—confirm burst nodes in eu-west-1 are healthy and added to routing pool.

ops-runner: eu-west-1 nodes up and registered. Routing table updated: 15% of spill traffic now eligible for eu-west-1.

kevin: For ABC-Corp, billing approval received via PM. Traffic shift in progress.

devon: Noting a small issue: one customer with large batched jobs hit backpressure and is retrying aggressively. I've added a per-job concurrency cap (4 -> 2) for them.

marta: Keep an eye for customer impact chatter in support channel. Notify if any SLA breaches look imminent.

sre-bot: [info] autoscaler: added 4 nodes to burst-pool-west, projected capacity +4 GPUs.

ops-runner: Also enabled temporary quota adjustment: `quotactl set --customer=heavy-xyz --limit=soft:50% --window=10m`

jen: Support notified. Posting canned message for affected customers with guidance about retry/backoff.

marta: TL;DR: soft caps applied to high-usage customers, cross-region spill enabled, burst nodes added in eu-west-1, ongoing monitoring. We'll keep this thread for timeline.

devon: I'll keep iterating caps and revert when node health >90% for 15 minutes.

kevin: After stablises, we should run a post-mortem on spot reclaim patterns and consider reserved capacity for critical SKUs.

marta: Agreed. For now, moving to monitoring loop. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
